cfgRescale.heading: CFG Rescale Multiplier
paragraphs: Rescale multiplier for CFG guidance, used for models trained using zero-terminal SNR (ztsnr).
Suggested value of 0.7 for these models.

cfgScale.heading: CFG Scale
paragraphs: Controls how much the prompt influences the generation process.
High CFG Scale values can result in over-saturation and distorted generation results.

clipSkip.heading: CLIP Skip
paragraphs: How many layers of the CLIP model to skip.
Certain models are better suited to be used with CLIP Skip.

colorCompensation.heading: Color Compensation
paragraphs: Adjust the input image to reduce color shifts during inpainting or img2img (SDXL Only).

concepts.heading: LoRA
paragraphs: Lightweight models that are used in conjunction with base models.

conditioningRebalance.heading: Conditioning rebalance
paragraphs: Krea 2 reads your prompt through twelve tapped layers of its text encoder and stacks them together. Each bar sets how much one of those layers counts.

Shallow taps, on the left, track the prompt's literal wording. Deep taps, on the right, track its meaning and composition. Raising the deep taps pushes the model harder toward what you asked for; raising the shallow taps holds it closer to how you phrased it.
Gain scales the whole stack afterwards, which counteracts the quality dilution from distillation. Leave both at the defaults unless prompt adherence is the problem you are solving.

conditioningRebalanceGain.heading: Rebalance gain
paragraphs: Overall gain applied to the conditioning after per-layer weighting. Higher values push harder toward the prompt.
Default is 4.0. Very high values may over-saturate or distort the output.

creativity.heading: Creativity
paragraphs: Creativity controls the amount of freedom granted to the model when adding details. Low creativity stays close to the original image, while high creativity allows for more change. When using a prompt, high creativity increases the influence of the prompt.

denoisingStrength.heading: Denoising Strength
paragraphs: Controls how much the generated image varies from the raster layers.
Lower strength stays closer to the combined visible raster layers. Higher strength relies more on the global prompt.
When there are no raster layers with visible content, this setting is ignored.

guidance.heading: Guidance
paragraphs: Controls how much the prompt influences the generation process.
High guidance values can result in over-saturation and high or low guidance may result in distorted generation results. Guidance only applies to FLUX DEV models.

height.heading: Height
paragraphs: Height of the generated image. Must be a multiple of 8.

dypePreset.heading: DyPE (High-Resolution)
paragraphs: Dynamic Position Extrapolation improves FLUX.1 generation quality at sizes above the 1024px training resolution.

Off: standard generation. Auto: enables above 1536px. Area: enables by image area. 4K: tuned for 4K output. Manual: set the magnitude (λs) and decay speed (λt) yourself; 2.0 suits 4K and above, 1.0 around 2K–3K, 0.5 just above 1024px.

encoderQuantization.heading: Encoder Quantization
paragraphs: Quantizes the Qwen2.5-VL text encoder on load to reduce VRAM use. 4-bit (nf4) saves the most memory; 8-bit (int8) is a middle ground. None keeps the bf16 weights.
A quantized encoder cannot stay in the model cache, so it is loaded from disk on every generation, twice when CFG is above 1. None keeps the cached encoder and loads it once.

styleStrength.heading: Style Strength
paragraphs: How strongly the reference's look is transferred. 1.0 is the recommended setting; 2.0 is a heavier effect and 0 turns the reference off.

krea2ReferenceMode.heading: Reference Mode
paragraphs: Style transfers one reference's look (palette, texture, rendering) while the prompt keeps driving the content. It needs no LoRA.

Edit is for Krea-2 edit LoRAs, such as the pose and depth LoRAs: the model reads up to three enabled references in card order and the prompt describes what to make of them. Without such a LoRA in Concepts the model copies the references. Edit references cannot be combined with a style reference or with regional guidance.

A single reference starts as Style. For an edit LoRA that takes one reference, such as a pose skeleton, switch it to Edit. Adding a second image turns a Style reference still at its default strength into Edit as well.
Some edit LoRAs, such as pose LoRAs trained with isolated references, also need Reference K/V cache under Advanced. Check the LoRA's model card.

krea2ReferenceKvCache.heading: Reference K/V Cache
paragraphs: For Krea-2 edit LoRAs trained with isolated references (ai-toolkit's kv_cache option), such as the thedeoxen Krea-2 pose LoRA. The references then run through the model once per generation instead of in every step, which is faster.

Leave it off for normal edit LoRAs. The LoRA file does not say which kind it is; check its model card. It applies only with Edit references and an edit LoRA in Concepts; otherwise it keeps its setting but is not used.

timestepShift.heading: Timestep Shift
paragraphs: Overrides the sigma-schedule shift. Left on auto the model derives it from the image size, which is recommended.
Qwen Image Lightning LoRAs are trained for a fixed shift of 3. Lower values spend more steps at low noise; higher values at high noise.

imageInfluence.heading: Image Influence
paragraphs: How strongly a FLUX Redux reference image steers the generation, from Lowest to Highest.
Lower settings leave more room for the prompt. Highest follows the reference most closely.

fluxReduxImageInfluence.heading: Image Influence
paragraphs: Controls how strongly the reference image influences the generated image.
Higher values keep the output closer to the reference image; lower values let the prompt drive more of the result.

hidiffusion.heading: HiDiffusion
paragraphs: Enables HiDiffusion denoising for higher-resolution generation.
Try at 1536px or higher for the most visible effect.

hidiffusionRauNet.heading: HiDiffusion: RAU-Net
paragraphs: Enables RAU-Net blocks used by HiDiffusion.
Can improve structure and detail at higher resolutions.

hidiffusionT1Ratio.heading: HiDiffusion: T1 Ratio
paragraphs: Controls the early switch point for HiDiffusion (T1).
Lower values switch earlier; higher values preserve global structure longer.

hidiffusionT2Ratio.heading: HiDiffusion: T2 Ratio
paragraphs: Controls the late switch point for HiDiffusion (T2).
Higher values keep window attention active longer.

hidiffusionWindowAttn.heading: HiDiffusion: Window Attention
paragraphs: Enables windowed attention used by HiDiffusion.
Can boost local detail, but may affect global coherence.

seedVariance.heading: Seed variance
paragraphs: Distilled few-step models like Krea-2-Turbo can produce nearly identical images across different seeds. This adds seed-based noise to the text embeddings to increase variation while staying reproducible.
Enable this to get more diverse results when exploring seeds, at some cost to prompt adherence.

seedVarianceRandomize.heading: Randomized channels
paragraphs: Percentage of embedding values that receive noise (0-100%); 0 disables.
Lower values create more selective perturbations, while 100% affects all values.

seedVarianceStrength.heading: Variance strength
paragraphs: Noise strength as a multiplier of the embedding's standard deviation, so it behaves consistently regardless of the embedding scale (including whether conditioning rebalance is on).
0 is off, 0.1 is subtle, 0.5 is strong. Higher values give more variety but drift further from the prompt.

layerStackControl.heading: Control Layers
paragraphs: Layers that guide generation with structural hints such as edges, depth, or pose maps.
Each control layer pairs its image with a control model and a weight that sets how strongly it steers the result.

layerStackInpaintMask.heading: Inpaint Masks
paragraphs: Masks that mark regions of the image for regeneration.
Painted areas are regenerated on the next invoke; noise and denoise-limit modifiers tune how strongly the area may change.

layerStackRaster.heading: Raster Layers
paragraphs: The pixel layers that compose your image and feed generation.
Layers apply top to bottom, and each can carry a stack of non-destructive adjustments such as levels, curves, or hue.

layerStackRegionalGuidance.heading: Regional Guidance
paragraphs: Regions that apply prompts and reference images to part of the image.
Painted regions scope their prompts and reference images to just that area of the canvas.

loraWeight.heading: LoRA Weight
paragraphs: Weight of the LoRA. Higher weight will lead to larger impacts on the final image.

mistralEncoder.heading: Mistral Encoder
paragraphs: FLUX.2 [dev] reads your prompt with the Mistral Small 3.1 text encoder. A single-file or GGUF checkpoint does not carry one, so it has to be selected here.

model.heading: Model
paragraphs: Model used for generation. Different models are trained to specialize in producing different aesthetic results and content.

negativePrompt.heading: Negative Prompt
paragraphs: The generation process avoids the concepts in the negative prompt. Use this to exclude qualities or objects from the output.
Compel attention weighting and embeddings work with SD 1.5, SD 2.x and SDXL only.

pidMode.heading: PiD Decode (Super-Resolution Decoder)
paragraphs: PiD replaces the standard VAE decode with NVIDIA's Pixel Diffusion Decoder, a diffusion-based 4x super-resolution decoder. It requires a PiD decoder model and a Gemma-2 caption encoder.
Fit: generate at your chosen resolution, PiD decodes it 4x, then downscales back to that size - extra detail at the same output size, and it composites onto the canvas (works for Image to Image too).

Native (4x): your dimensions are the 4x target. Generation runs at a quarter of them (e.g. 512 -> 2048) and PiD's full 4x output is used directly. The PiD decoders are trained for 2K output (512px sources), with 2K-to-4K variants for 4K.
Because PiD's diffusion decode reconstructs detail, you can usually lower the generation Steps to save time. 'Scale Before Processing' must be set to None while PiD is enabled.

positivePrompt.heading: Positive Prompt
paragraphs: Guides the generation process. You may use any words or phrases.
Dynamic Prompts syntax works with every model. Compel attention weighting and embeddings work with SD 1.5, SD 2.x and SDXL only.

qwen35Encoder.heading: Qwen3.5 Encoder
paragraphs: Anima-3.8B's prompt adapter also reads a Qwen3.5 4B text encoder. The checkpoint does not carry one, so it has to be selected here.

qwen3Encoder.heading: Qwen3 Encoder
paragraphs: Z-Image, FLUX.2 Klein and Anima read your prompt with a Qwen3 text encoder: Z-Image and Klein 4B with the 4B, Klein 9B with the 8B, Anima with the 0.6B. A bare checkpoint does not carry one, so it has to be selected here.

qwen3VlEncoder.heading: Qwen3-VL Encoder
paragraphs: Krea-2 reads your prompt with the Qwen3-VL 4B text encoder. A single-file or GGUF checkpoint does not carry one, so it has to be selected here.
Krea-2 edit references are read by the encoder's vision weights, which a GGUF encoder does not have.

qwenVlEncoder.heading: Qwen VL Encoder
paragraphs: Qwen Image reads your prompt with the Qwen2.5-VL text encoder. A GGUF or single-file checkpoint does not carry one, so it has to be selected here.

referenceImage.heading: Global Reference Image
paragraphs: Applies a reference image to influence the entire generation.

referenceImageStrength.heading: Reference Image Strength
paragraphs: How much of the reference character the generation carries. 0 turns the reference off.
Higher values carry more of the character's hair, outfit and accessories, and also more of the reference's composition and content.

referenceImageWeight.heading: Reference Image Weight
paragraphs: How strongly this reference image steers the generation.
Lower weight treats it as a loose suggestion; higher weight holds the output closer to the reference.

scheduler.heading: Scheduler
paragraphs: Scheduler used during the generation process.
Each scheduler defines how to iteratively add noise to an image or how to update a sample based on a model's output.

seamlessTiling.heading: Seamless Tiling
paragraphs: Generates an image that tiles without visible seams.
Enable each axis independently to tile horizontally, vertically, or both.

seed.heading: Seed
paragraphs: Controls the starting noise used for generation.
Disable the "Random" option to produce identical results with the same generation settings.

stepRange.heading: Begin / End Step Percentage
paragraphs: This setting determines which portion of the denoising (generation) process incorporates this guidance.
• Start Step (%): Specifies when to begin applying this guidance during the generation process.
• End Step (%): Specifies when to stop applying this guidance and revert to general guidance from the model and other settings.

steps.heading: Steps
paragraphs: Number of steps that will be performed in each generation.
Higher step counts will typically create better images but will require more generation time.

structure.heading: Structure
paragraphs: Structure controls how closely the output image will keep to the layout of the original. Low structure allows major changes, while high structure strictly maintains the original composition and layout.

clipEmbed.heading: CLIP Embed
paragraphs: FLUX.1 pairs its T5 encoder with a CLIP text encoder. A bare FLUX checkpoint does not carry one, so it must be chosen explicitly.

t5Encoder.heading: T5 Encoder
paragraphs: FLUX.1 reads your prompt with a T5 text encoder. Most FLUX transformers ship as a bare checkpoint and cannot supply one, so it has to be selected here.

tileControlNet.heading: ControlNet
paragraphs: ControlNets provide guidance to the generation process, helping create images with controlled composition, structure, or style, depending on the model selected.

tileOverlap.heading: Tile Overlap
paragraphs: Controls the overlap between adjacent tiles during upscaling. Higher overlap values help reduce visible seams between tiles but use more memory.
The default value of 128 works well for most cases, but you can adjust based on your specific needs and memory constraints.

tileSize.heading: Tile Size
paragraphs: Controls the size of tiles used during the upscaling process. Larger tiles use more memory but may produce better results.
SD1.5 models default to 768, while SDXL models default to 1024. Reduce tile size if you encounter memory issues.

upscaleModel.heading: Upscale Model
paragraphs: The upscale model scales the image to the output size before details are added. Any supported upscale model may be used, but some are specialized for different kinds of images, like photos or line drawings.

upscaleScale.heading: Scale
paragraphs: Scale controls the output image size, and is based on a multiple of the input image resolution. For example a 2x upscale on a 1024x1024 image would produce a 2048 x 2048 output.

vae.heading: VAE
paragraphs: Model used for translating AI output into the final image.

vaePrecision.heading: VAE Precision
paragraphs: The precision used during VAE encoding and decoding.
Fp16/Half precision is more efficient, at the expense of minor image variations.

width.heading: Width
paragraphs: Width of the generated image. Must be a multiple of 8.

refinerModel.heading: Refiner model
paragraphs: An SDXL Refiner model that takes over the last part of the denoising schedule from the SDXL base model, adding fine detail.
Only SDXL Refiner models are listed here; they cannot be used as the main model.

refinerSteps.heading: Refiner steps
paragraphs: Number of steps the refiner schedule is divided into. Only the part after Refiner start runs.

refinerCfgScale.heading: Refiner CFG
paragraphs: How strictly the refiner follows the prompt during its pass, like the main CFG.

refinerScheduler.heading: Refiner scheduler
paragraphs: Scheduler used for the refiner pass, independent of the base model's scheduler.

refinerStart.heading: Refiner start
paragraphs: Where in the schedule the base model hands over to the refiner.
0.8 means the base model denoises the first 80% and the refiner finishes the last 20%; 0 hands the whole schedule to the refiner, and 1 leaves it nothing to do, so the refiner is not run.
On the Canvas the base pass cannot start after the hand-over, so an image-to-image strength above 1 − Refiner start is capped there.

refinerAestheticScore.heading: Aesthetic score
paragraphs: The refiner was trained with an aesthetic rating from 1 to 10. The positive score steers the result toward images rated that highly; the negative score steers it away from images rated that low.

componentSlots.h3ComponentSourceHelp: Required: a Diffusers MiniMax H3 install (full or components-only) provides the tokenizer, processor, and VAEs the single-file transformer does not carry.
componentSlots.h3HybridBaseHelp: Optional: an FL2VA transformer to run with this Ref2VA model’s AdaLN projections. This improves the video quality at the cost of some loss of reference fidelity.
componentSlots.h3TextEncoderCheckpointHelp: Required when the Model Components install is components-only (no text-encoder weights); a full install provides its own.
componentSlots.h3TextEncoderOptionalHelp: Optional single-file Qwen3-VL encoder used in place of the main model’s text encoder.
componentSlots.h3TextEncoderRequiredHelp: Required: this install has no text-encoder weights, so the text encoder must come from a single-file Qwen3-VL checkpoint.
componentSlots.ltx2ComponentSourceHelp: The LTX-2 components install supplying the VAEs, vocoder and text connectors.
componentSlots.ltx2DurationHeadHelp: Optional. Predicts how long the shot your prompt describes should run, so Auto duration can set the length.
componentSlots.ltx2TextEncoderHelp: LTX-2’s Gemma-4 text encoder. Required: no LTX-2 model carries one.
componentSlots.wanComponentSourceHelp: Select a Diffusers Wan model to provide VAE and text-encoder components.
componentSlots.wanLowNoiseHelp: Optional second A14B expert. Without it the high-noise expert runs the whole schedule.
componentSlots.wanOptionalWithSourceHelp: Required unless a Diffusers component source is available.

video.negativeCfgHelp: Used only when CFG is greater than 1.
video.noLoras: No concepts added. Compatible LoRAs adjust style and motion.
video.hybridStartBlockHelp: Blocks from here through 49 keep this Ref2VA model’s AdaLN projections; earlier blocks use the FL2VA base. Lower values follow references more closely at more of Ref2VA’s quality cost; 25 is the recommended balance.
video.acceleratorBrokenDescription: One of its LoRAs was removed or disabled, so steps and CFG were restored to the model's defaults.
video.acceleratorSwitched: {{label}} now running on a different LoRA

video.framesFromClip: The conditioning clip decides the length.
video.fpsFromClip: The generation runs at the conditioning clip's frame rate.
video.audioCfgHelp: How hard the soundtrack follows the prompt. LTX-2 guides audio far harder than picture.
